label: rem:madelung-fluid
title: Madelung transformation: quantum fluid and vortex filaments
html:
The Madelung split. Decomposing \psi = \sqrt{\rho}\exp(JS/\hbar_q) separates the q-deformed Schrödinger equation into two real equations. Setting the velocity v = \nabla_A S and fluid density \rho = |\psi|^2 yields:

  • Continuity: \partial_t \rho + \nabla_A\cdot(\rho v) = 0.
  • Quantum Euler equation:
  \partial_t v + (v\cdot\nabla_A)v
  =  -\nabla_A\!\left(\frac{\delta\mathcal{H}}{\delta\rho}\right)
  -  \nabla_A Q_q,
  \qquad
  Q_q =  -\frac{\hbar_q^2}{2}\frac{\Delta_q\sqrt{\rho}}{\sqrt{\rho}},

where Q_q is the q-deformed quantum pressure.

|\psi|^2 as fluid density; q as brane thickness. The substrate parameter q modulates the effective thickness of the quantum fluid. Near q \approx 1, the quantum pressure vanishes (Q_q \approx 0) and the system reduces to ordinary inviscid flow. At q \gg 1, Q_q dominates; the fluid strongly resists compression. This resistance acts as the inertial mass of the brane.

Zero-information state |\psi|^2 = 0. The vacuum \psi = 0 carries no medium, no vortex, and no fermion. It lies outside the support of all harmonic modes filtered by the algebraic filter. As q \to 1, \hbar_q \to 0: the vacuum represents the state of maximal classical certainty.

Geodesics as stable vortex filaments. Bosonic modes follow straight null geodesics of the acoustic metric g_{\mathrm{ac}}. Fermionic modes spiral around the zeros of \psi, forming stable vortex filaments \varrho whose mass follows

  m  \propto  \oint_\varrho \|\nabla_A q\|\cdot\|L \wedge F^+\|,

reproducing the mass identity as a line integral of the substrate curvature around the vortex core.
